research_mode: official ONS and Home Office sources only; current YE March 2026 offence composition, coverage, trend, data-quality and outcome-timing controls; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: CSEW violence peak comparison
verified_claims: violence with or without injury was 78% lower than the year ending December 1995 peak of 4.5 million
limitations: survey design and period labels must be retained

sources.name: Stranger violence prevalence
verified_claims: 0.7% of people aged 16 or over reported violence by a stranger
limitations: the estimate excludes populations outside private households

sources.name: Acquaintance violence prevalence
verified_claims: 0.4% of people aged 16 or over reported violence by an acquaintance
limitations: domestic violence is not adequately captured by the interviewer-administered measure

sources.name: Recorded violence without injury
verified_claims: police recorded violence without injury increased 2% to 829,017 offences
limitations: recording improvements make the series unsuitable as a pure trend measure

sources.name: Recorded violence with injury
verified_claims: police recorded violence with injury decreased 3% to 507,169 offences

sources.name: Latest available domestic abuse prevalence
verified_claims: the latest available CSEW estimate was 7.8% in year ending March 2025
this represented around 3.8 million people
limitations: year ending March 2026 estimates were deferred for further quality assurance

sources.name: Domestic-abuse-related recorded offences
verified_claims: police categorised 834,256 offences as domestic-abuse-related
the previous-year figure was 816,493
limitations: recorded offences do not measure domestic abuse prevalence

sources.name: Domestic-abuse-related violence count
verified_claims: 643,061 domestic-abuse-related offences were violence against the person offences
limitations: the count is an administrative classification, not a victim prevalence estimate

sources.name: Recorded sexual offences
verified_claims: police recorded sexual offences increased 4% to 217,567 from 209,114
limitations: recording improvements, new offences and increased reporting affect the trend

sources.name: Recorded rape offences
verified_claims: police recorded rape offences increased 4% to 74,727 from 71,614
limitations: recorded counts are not a prevalence measure

sources.name: Rape share of sexual offences
verified_claims: rape offences represented around 34% of police recorded sexual offences
limitations: the share depends on offence classification and reporting

sources.name: Latest available stalking prevalence
verified_claims: the latest available CSEW stalking estimate was 2.9% in year ending March 2025
this represented around 1.4 million people
limitations: year ending March 2026 stalking estimates were deferred

sources.name: Police recorded theft total
verified_claims: police recorded 1.6 million theft offences
this was an 8% decrease from 1.8 million
limitations: reporting and recording practices vary by theft type

sources.name: Vehicle offences
verified_claims: police recorded vehicle offences decreased 11% to 312,250
limitations: the count is not adjusted for vehicle population

sources.name: Recorded burglary
verified_claims: police recorded burglary decreased 9% to 223,456
the category includes residential and non-residential burglary
limitations: subcategories should be retained for interpretation
